This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the LaGuardia Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 2 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=klga

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**The near-certain market-implied odds for a 74–75 °F high on September 2, 2026, in New York City reflect the official National Weather Service observation from the primary Central Park station (or equivalent designated site) that recorded a daily maximum in that narrow band.** 

Hourly data showed temperatures climbing from overnight lows near 67 °F to an afternoon peak of 72–74 °F under mostly cloudy skies with light easterly flow and surface pressures around 30.05–30.08 inHg, preventing stronger daytime heating. This outcome sits well below the 1991–2020 climatological normal high of ~80–81 °F for the date, consistent with a cooler air mass and limited insolation. 

Because the market resolves strictly on the verified observational maximum (typically the highest 5-minute or hourly reading certified by NOAA/NWS), traders rapidly converged on the precise bin once preliminary climatological reports and station data became available on September 2–3. Only an official revision to the certified maximum—highly unlikely once quality-controlled data are released—could alter the result.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Official forecasts from the Hong Kong Observatory (HKO) set the daily maximum temperature range for September 3, 2026, at 26–31°C under northwest winds of 4–5 (locally stronger offshore and on high ground), partly cloudy skies with brief sunshine, and a low-to-moderate chance of one or two showers.** This positions 31°C as the leading outcome (market-implied ~52.5%), consistent with the upper bound of the official guidance and recent model consensus.

The primary scientific drivers include the lingering influence of tropical cyclone Sadul (crossing eastern Guangdong coastal areas) combined with the northeast monsoon, which maintains moderate northwest flow, limits strong solar heating through variable cloud cover, and supports isolated convective showers that can cap peak temperatures. Historical September climatology for Hong Kong shows typical daily maxima near 30–32°C under similar monsoon-influenced patterns, but the current setup—with dew points around 21–22°C and relative humidity 55–85%—favors values near the forecast ceiling rather than extremes.

Recent data reinforce this positioning: prior-day observations (September 2) reached ~31–32°C under comparable conditions, while today’s early readings and hourly model runs (e.g., temperatures climbing toward 29–30°C by midday with continued NW flow) align with a high near 31°C. Lower probabilities for 32°C or above (~19.5% and 1.8%) reflect the moderating effects of clouds and showers, while 30°C (~24.5%) remains plausible if convection develops earlier. Updated HKO briefings and model runs through the day will be the key near-term catalysts for any shifts in trader-implied odds.

This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Shanghai Pudong International Airport Station in degrees Celsius on 3 Sep '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=zspd

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event that there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to Metric Units" button until the relevant table displays °C.

This market will resolve once the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source, or by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, whichever comes first.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Clear skies, light winds, and strong September insolation in Chongqing’s subtropical basin climate are the main drivers pushing market-implied odds toward a 34–35 °C daily maximum.** Official forecasts from sources including the Chongqing Meteorological Observatory, Yr.no, and international models converge on a peak of 32–35 °C under mostly sunny to partly cloudy conditions, with minimal precipitation risk (under 5 %). Light northeasterly to easterly winds (generally 1–3 m/s) limit mixing and allow surface heating to build through the afternoon, while typical early-September humidity levels (40–60 %) moderate but do not strongly cap the high.

The narrow spread between 34 °C (45.5 %) and 35 °C (37 %) reflects residual uncertainty in exact peak timing, localized urban heat-island effects across districts, and minor model differences in boundary-layer moisture or thin high-cloud cover. A 33 °C outcome (14.5 %) would require more cloudiness or slightly stronger winds than currently indicated, while probabilities for 36 °C or higher remain low (around 5 %) because climatological early-September maxima rarely exceed the mid-30s without stronger subsidence or drier air. Traders are therefore weighting the balance of recent model consensus and historical analogs for a maximum in the narrow 34–35 °C window.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models and real-time observations position a peak of 31–33°C as the most probable range for Beijing’s highest temperature on September 3, 2026, aligning with the market’s leading implied probabilities (32°C at 47.5%, 31°C at 25.5%, 33°C at 19%).**

Multiple authoritative forecasts, including those from GFS-derived sources and local meteorological services, consistently project a daytime maximum near 32°C under mostly clear to sunny skies, light southerly or variable winds (2–4 mph), and low precipitation risk (under 5%). This reflects typical early-September conditions: sufficient solar insolation for daytime heating after overnight lows around 19–22°C, combined with moderate humidity (40–50%) that supports efficient surface warming without excessive evaporative cooling.

The implied probabilities cluster tightly because ensemble guidance shows limited spread in peak values, with 32°C emerging as the central tendency—slightly above the 1991–2020 climatological average high of ~28.6°C but well below the all-time September 3 record of 33.1°C. Minor model differences in cloud cover timing or exact wind shifts explain the secondary weight on 31°C and 33°C. No recent atmospheric developments, such as unusual blocking patterns or moisture surges, have shifted expectations away from this consensus range.

Recent conditions feature northwest winds of 2–4 m/s, high humidity (70–85%), and dew points near 22–23°C, which limit daytime heating. Multiple sources indicate a forecast high near 30°C under mostly cloudy to overcast skies with thunder showers or light rain possible, consistent with the active monsoon-influenced pattern typical for early September in the Pearl River Delta. 

The tight spread between 30°C and 31°C reflects uncertainty in exactly how much solar radiation reaches the surface: brief sun breaks could allow peaks near 31°C, while steadier cloudiness or precipitation would cap the maximum at 30°C. Higher outcomes (32°C+) carry low probability due to the cooling effect of moisture and limited insolation, while lower values remain unlikely given baseline warmth and urban heat retention in Shenzhen. 

Upcoming hourly observations and any updated model runs will clarify whether the day trends toward the upper or lower end of this narrow band.

Afternoon convection and associated cloud cover represent the key uncertainty, as stronger or earlier storms could cap temperatures in the upper 80s by reducing solar insolation and enhancing evaporative cooling, while delayed or weaker activity would allow readings to reach the low 90s consistent with the seasonal climatological average of 93°F. High boundary-layer moisture and weak steering flow further modulate the outcome by influencing storm timing and coverage, producing the tight clustering of market-implied probabilities around 86–91°F.

eventMetadata.context_description: **Forecast models converge on a peak of 29–30°C under clear skies and light northeasterly flow.** Multiple sources, including WeatherBug (85°F/29.4°C), Yr.no (30°C), and local Chinese services (20–30°C), show sunny conditions with minimal cloud cover and dew points supporting efficient daytime heating but moderated by 45–55% humidity and 5–10 mph winds. Minor model spreads—some runs peaking near 28.7°C while others reach 30–31°C—stem from subtle differences in boundary-layer mixing and exact timing of the daily maximum, keeping 29°C and 30°C nearly tied in trader pricing. Historical September averages for Zhengzhou (around 27–28°C highs) provide context, but the current stable high-pressure pattern and lack of frontal activity support the market’s tight clustering. Updated model runs and official observations later today will determine resolution within the narrow 28–31°C band.

**Northwesterly winds and a forecast clearing trend after morning showers are the main drivers positioning 17–18°C as the leading outcomes for Wellington’s daily maximum on September 4.** 

Local forecasts, including from NZ sources, indicate a high near 17°C with showers easing to fine conditions in the afternoon under strengthening northwesterlies. These conditions favor modest warming despite cloud and precipitation, as the flow draws milder air and allows some solar heating once skies clear. Official and model guidance clusters around 15–17°C, with a few runs reaching 18°C if clearing occurs earlier or winds enhance downslope warming. 

The market’s heavy weighting toward 18°C (56%) and 17°C (34.5%) reflects trader consensus on this range, incorporating recent forecast updates that emphasize the northwest regime and afternoon improvement. Lower probabilities for 16°C or below align with limited downside risk from persistent rain or stronger onshore flow, while outcomes above 19°C remain marginal given seasonal norms and model spread. Updated model runs and any MetService briefing on wind strength or timing of clearance represent the key near-term catalysts that could shift these implied probabilities.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Persistent monsoon rains and associated cloud cover are the dominant factors capping maximum temperatures in Lucknow around 30–32°C for September 4, aligning with the market’s heaviest weighting on 31°C (45%) and 32°C (21.5%).**

A low-pressure system over the Bay of Bengal region continues to steer moisture into Uttar Pradesh, sustaining overcast skies, scattered thunderstorms, and high humidity that limit solar heating. Official observations from September 2 recorded a maximum of 30.5°C (three degrees below normal) after heavy overnight rainfall, with similar suppressed readings across nearby districts. Short-range models (IMD, Met Office, and others) converge on highs of 30–33°C for September 4 amid continued 70–90% rain probabilities, while longer-term climatology shows September averages near 32–33°C before the typical post-monsoon rise. Recent model runs have not shown significant warming trends, keeping trader consensus clustered on the 30–32°C band rather than higher outliers.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent model consensus from European and global forecasting centers points to a strengthening low-pressure system and associated frontal boundary driving increased cloud cover, southwest winds, and moderate rainfall across Warsaw on September 4, limiting daytime solar heating and capping the maximum temperature. Forecasts from sources including the Polish Institute of Meteorology and Water Management and international ensembles consistently show highs near 20–22 °C under mostly overcast skies, aligning with the market’s leading implied probabilities for 21 °C (39 %), 20 °C (26 %), and 22 °C (23.5 %). This represents a modest cooldown from the clearer, warmer conditions of September 2–3. Updated runs through early September 3 reinforce the precipitation signal, reducing upside risk for 23 °C or higher while keeping lower outcomes (19 °C or below) unlikely absent a sharper cold-air surge.

**Recent clearing after frontal rains positions 31–33°C as the core range for Wuhan's September 4 high.** 

Official forecasts from the Wuhan Meteorological Observatory and multiple models show sunny to mostly clear skies on the 4th following light rain and northerly winds on the 2nd–3rd, with highs projected at 30–33°C (roughly 86–91°F). This aligns with early-September climatology, where long-term averages sit near 28–31°C and historical extremes rarely exceed 36°C this early in the month. 

Northeasterly flow and moderating humidity after the frontal passage favor modest daytime heating without strong subsidence or clear-sky amplification that would push temperatures higher. Ensemble guidance shows tight clustering in the low-to-mid 30s°C, with limited upside risk from model spread or unexpected clearing. Market-implied odds therefore concentrate on 32°C and 33°C as the most probable outcomes, reflecting aggregated trader assessment of official agency guidance and short-range model consensus.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent official forecasts from multiple meteorological services converge on a maximum temperature of 19–20°C for Cape Town on September 4, supporting the market’s heavy weighting toward those outcomes. A strong southeasterly flow under clearing high pressure following Thursday’s rain and cooler conditions is expected to deliver abundant sunshine and dry air, with dew points falling into the single digits Celsius and minimal cloud cover. These factors, combined with typical early-spring insolation and downslope warming along the Cape Peninsula, favor a modest daily rise above the seasonal average near 18°C. Model agreement remains high with limited spread, though any unexpected increase in low-level moisture or wind shift could trim the peak by 1°C. Updated guidance from the South African Weather Service and global ensembles will provide the final calibration before resolution.
